clue.text: Put back a receptacle in side feature of a hotel room?

indicators.note: putting something back sends it the way it came, so the letters run in the opposite direction
to sit in something is to be held inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a rim is the side or edge of a vessel
taken as written
a bin is a container for rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone tidying a hotel room returns a little bin to its place beside the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' is a noun for an edge, not the side of the room; the whole assembly is read backwards at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotel rooms commonly come with a small stocked fridge of drinks and snacks for guests.

clue.text: Word from Paris now devised for a style of music

indicators.note: something devised is invented or worked out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: mot is French for word
these three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French word coined in the present day to label a musical genre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' points to French; 'from Paris' tells you to translate 'word'.
explanation.definitionFit: Motown is the soul and pop sound associated with the Detroit record label founded by Berry Gordy.

clue.text: Observing number given money? Good

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
tin is old slang for money
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone watches a performer handed cash and approves.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin as money is dated British slang; the question mark and full stop break the clue into three small pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to observe or take notice of it, so the participles match.

clue.text: Errand best put off for those serving drinks

indicators.note: something put off is disturbed or thrown out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A task is best postponed by people who are busy pouring drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put off' reads as postpone, but it is telling you to rearrange the ten letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: People who mix and pour drinks behind a pub or cocktail counter are known by this job title.

clue.text: Note group having to adjust again

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: A band has to retune its instruments once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Notes of the sol-fa scale (do, re, mi...) are a common source of short letter groups.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something is to adjust it, and doing that a second time is setting it once more.

clue.text: Range for picking up others?

parts.note: surface reading: the distance over which someone could collect other people, like a lift or pickup
setter's reading: picking up means hearing, so this is the distance at which other people can be heard

explanation.walkthrough: 'Picking up' suggests giving people a lift; here it means catching their voices.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the distance within which a sound or voice can be heard.

clue.text: Last of police force accepting small measure as feature of the online world?

indicators.note: the last of something is its final element, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of police

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: to coerce is to force
mm is the abbreviation for millimetre, a small measure

explanation.surface: A police force adopting a minor policy as part of its online presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' reads as the police force, but it is a verb meaning to compel.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying and selling over the internet is a central part of online life and trade.

clue.text: Hasten with throng avoiding cold

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep away from it, so that letter is left out

parts.note: a crush is a dense crowd
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Hurrying along with a crowd while trying not to catch a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: CRUSH without its C leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are verbs meaning to move or act with great speed.

clue.text: Trouble with argument about entry to hectic airport

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so the outer pieces wrap around

parts.note: heat means trouble or pressure, as in 'the heat is on'

indicators.note: the entry to a word is where you go in, its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of hectic
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: Tempers flare in a busy airport terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAT and ROW together surround the H. Heathrow is London's main airport.
explanation.definitionFit: London's largest international hub is a specific example of a place where planes land and depart.

clue.text: Illegally enter resort with sun twice after three in Sicily?

parts.note: tre is Italian for three, and Sicily is part of Italy
a spa is a resort town
S is the abbreviation for sun, given two times

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker sneaks into a Sicilian resort after spending days in the sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the resort and the two suns behind the Italian number.
explanation.definitionFit: To go onto land or property without permission is a legal wrong of unlawful entry.

clue.text: One giving instruction thus regularly rejected rubbish

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: first and third letters of thus

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so its letters run the other way

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A teacher thus repeatedly dismisses a pupil's work as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' asks for alternate letters of the word it follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A private teacher who coaches individuals or small groups is someone who gives lessons.

clue.text: In a merry state, saw scope to include new festive scene

indicators.note: to include something is to take it in among the rest, so a letter joins inside
a merry, tipsy state is a muddled one, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: eight letters to rearrange
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy at a party looks through a telescope at a wintry Christmas view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a merry state' sounds like a description of a person, but it signals rearranging SAW SCOPE once N is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape covered in snow is the kind of wintry view seen on Christmas cards.

clue.text: Women put in ground with draw to entice mass in December?

indicators.note: to entice is to lure someone in, so one piece is brought inside another

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
to inter is to bury
a tie is a drawn game
M is the abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: Women at a burial try to tempt people to a church mass at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' suggests a church service but is the physics symbol M, held inside TIE.
explanation.definitionFit: December is an example of the cold season in the northern hemisphere, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Ask for quiet work in retail outlet

parts.note: sh is what you say to ask for quiet
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A manager wants silence on the job in a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ask for quiet' gives the hushing sound itself, not a word meaning quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A store selling goods to the public is the standard sense of the word.

clue.text: American stops a tense period only with difficulty

indicators.note: something that stops a gap plugs it, sitting inside the opening

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
a stretch is a period of time
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American calms a tense period with some effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stops' means plugs: the American A goes into the gap between A T and STRETCH.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something just about achievable when one makes an extra effort.

clue.text: Co-ordinates in order to get baubles and tinsel?

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: eleven letters to rearrange, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Someone arranges matching items in a sequence to deck out the Christmas tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Co-ordinates' looks like a verb about matching, but it is the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Baubles and tinsel are examples of ornaments hung on a Christmas tree, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Jointly founded centre to host hundred on uncertain date

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so one piece is placed inside another
in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the pieces follow in sequence

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
these four letters are rearranged

indicators.note: something uncertain is unsettled, so these letters are not in fixed order

parts.note: the core is the centre

explanation.surface: A co-founded centre plans to host a hundred guests on a date not yet fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: CORE holds C to make COCRE, followed by a rearranged DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-create is to bring something into being together, so jointly founding something matches the past tense.

clue.text: Where one might see students with a learner of a casual sort

parts.note: students sit in a form, a school class
taken as written
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A relaxed type of learner found among students.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group, so students are found 'in form'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something relaxed and not bound by convention or ceremony is casual in nature.

clue.text: Sets idly disposed are given a distinctive designation?

indicators.note: things disposed are set out or arranged, so the letters take up a new order

parts.note: eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Stage sets lazily arranged are given a special label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Idly' looks like the manner of disposal, but it belongs to the letters; 'disposed' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stylised is rendered in a particular conventional manner, marked by a distinctive form or label.

clue.text: Enthusiast of a crazy sort for seasonal food accessories?

parts.note: a nut is a keen fan
crackers is British slang for mad

explanation.surface: A wildly keen fan of Christmas kitchen gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: Crackers, meaning crazy, is everyday British slang; it also hints at Christmas crackers.
explanation.definitionFit: The tool for opening shells is a Christmas table item, since bowls of nuts are traditional at that season.

clue.text: Look around edges of thicket for a glove

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: mien is a person's look or bearing

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

parts.note: first and last letters of thicket

explanation.surface: Searching the edge of the undergrowth for a lost glove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look' is the noun meaning appearance, not the verb; MIEN wraps the two Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitten is a kind of hand covering with one section for the four fingers, so it is a type of glove.

clue.text: Opinion from left-wingers in straitened times almost never carefully examined

indicators.note: the left wing of each word is its leftmost end, so the opening letters are kept

parts.words: straitened times almost never carefully examined
parts.note: the opening letters of six consecutive words

explanation.surface: A view held by socialists during austerity that went largely unscrutinised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left-wingers' suggests socialists, but it means the left-hand letters of the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a standpoint or attitude taken on an issue, so it is a synonym for a view held.

clue.text: Solitary old liberal found in US city

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: something found in a place is inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: NY is New York
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A lonely ageing progressive living in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: O comes first, then L goes inside NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe the single one of its kind, as in an only child or a solitary survivor.

clue.text: Go when given licence to acquire northern flavoured sweet

parts.note: go and pep both mean energy or drive

indicators.note: to acquire something is to take it in, so one piece ends up inside another

parts.note: a permit is a licence
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A trip north once the paperwork is sorted, with a sweet treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is a noun meaning energy, as in 'full of go', not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint-flavoured confectionery is commonly named after the herb used to flavour it.

clue.text: Sound of tranquillity in musical work

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is spoken, so we want a different spelling with that pronunciation

parts.note: peace means tranquillity

explanation.surface: Hearing calm in a quiet passage of music.
explanation.walkthrough: PEACE and PIECE are pronounced identically.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition, such as a piano piece, is a standard term for a single work of music.

clue.text: Proposal put in limp language

indicators.note: something put in other words is lodged inside them, so the answer lies within the text

parts.note: the end of limp and start of language

explanation.surface: A suggestion expressed in feeble wording.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the gap between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme or suggested course of action is a proposal put forward for consideration.

clue.text: Fancy item lost close to store is evergreen at Christmas

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or imagined, so the letters are worked into a new pattern

parts.note: eight letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the close of a word is where it finishes, so the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of store

explanation.surface: A decorative object went missing near the shop that sells Christmas greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy item' reads as a decorative object, but 'Fancy' is the signal and ITEM LOST plus E are the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This parasitic plant keeps its leaves all year and is hung up at Christmas for kissing under.

clue.text: From the East some man, a titled figure of great importance

indicators.note: coming from the east means travelling westward, right to left in an across clue
some of the text means only part of it, so the letters lie inside the words

parts.note: consecutive letters spanning the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A man from the East, a nobleman, who is a major figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Read right to left inside 'man, a tit' to find the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A titan, after the giant gods of Greek myth, is a person of enormous power or influence.

clue.text: Was first around Middle East city, bearing a lot of stuff?

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: to lead is to be first; led is its past tense
Aden is a port city in Yemen

explanation.surface: A traveller who led the way around a Yemeni port was carrying heavy baggage.
explanation.walkthrough: Aden is a port in Yemen. The answer is a rare variant of laden, from the old verb lade, to load.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laden is weighed down with a heavy load, so it is carrying plenty of goods.

clue.text: Improve getting two directions by luck, first off

indicators.note: with the first taken off, the opening letter is removed

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
chance is luck

explanation.surface: Getting better at navigating by sheer fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First off' applies only to luck; the compass points stay whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance is to raise the quality or value of something, making it better.
